title: Creating a base Django project
author: Peter
content:
Our first milestone is to set up a workflow between our local environment and PythonAnywhere.  We are not going to add any functionality at this point - just the skeleton application.

 

Install Django

From a bash terminal (either in VS Code or an ordinary terminal session) in the project base directory, ensure the virtual environment is activated and install Django.

pip install django

Note that if this is the first time you have used pip in the virtual environment then you may get prompted to upgrade pip itself.  This is not essential but probably worth doing if only to stop the warnings appearing.

python3 -m pip install --upgrade pip

Initialise the Django Project

Again in the terminal window in the parent to the root directory of the project and with the virtual environment activated:

django-admin startproject <projectname> <directory-name>

Test the Django installation

Go into the project root directory (the one containing  manage.py) and start the server (note that this will tie up this window while the server is running).

python3 manage.py runserver

You will receive a response something like the following:

(virtenv) (base) peter@Peters-MacBook-Pro-3 sbs % python manage.py runserver

Run 'python manage.py migrate' to apply them.
